notes: Whose is read as the fusion of the predicative le with the interrogative mi (rule 30), the copula joining that fused unit under rule 49's closing sentences; the competing reading would give is to the noun na'arah, but that noun is the clause's subject rather than its predicate.
Both articles of ha-na'arah ha-zot are unrepresented: the ASV writes no the for the phrase, and the demonstrative pronoun holds the only word written for it (rules 41, 47).
